text:
The Jets traded Connor Hellebuyck, and on Saturday they see him again: Daily Faceoff reports he starts for New Jersey against his former team for the first time since the deal. It is the obvious headline, but the more surprising story is how well Winnipeg is doing without him. The Jets are 8-1-1 over their last ten and have won three straight with 63% of the expected goals in those games.

Stuart Skinner has been a big part of that. His save percentage looks ordinary, but against the hard shots he has been .923 over his last five starts, 4.9 goals saved above expected. Mark Scheifele set the franchise's all-time goals record during the run, and Kyle Connor keeps scoring. The Scheifele and Connor line, with Gabriel Vilardi or Cole Perfetti on the right, has outscored opponents 24-15 over those two combinations. Viggo Bjorck, still a teenager, ranks among the league's top rookies.

Over the full season, though, Winnipeg is a .500 team on process: 49.6% of the expected goals and 48% at five on five, with goals at both ends close to the chances. Our numbers say the Jets have about three more points than they earned. The depth is thin; the Dawson Mercer, Perfetti and Brayden Yager line gets only 41% of the expected goals.

Our numbers give Winnipeg a 46% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether the recent shot share sticks, because the hot stretch is the first time all season the Jets have controlled play for more than a few games.
